title: Supremum of absolute set-integrals of a mean-zero function
statement:
Let $\mu$ be a finite measure on a measurable space $\Omega$, and let $g \colon \Omega \to \bbr$ be measurable and integrable with mean zero, $\int_\Omega g\,d\mu = 0$. Then the supremum of $\abs{\int_S g\,d\mu}$ taken over all measurable sets $S \subseteq \Omega$ equals the integral of $g$ over the region where it is nonnegative:
\[
  \sup_{S\text{ measurable}} \abs*{\int_S g\,d\mu} \;=\; \int_{\{x \,:\, g(x) \ge 0\}} g\,d\mu.
\]
hypotheses_covered: μ is a finite measure on Ω
g is integrable with respect to μ
g has mean zero (integral of g is 0)
supremum ranges over all measurable sets S
replaced:
Let $\mu$ be a finite measure and $g$ measurable, integrable, and mean-zero.  Then
\[
  \sup_{S\text{ measurable}}\Bigl|\int_S g\,d\mu\Bigr|
  \;=\; \int_{\{g \ge 0\}} g\,d\mu.
\]
